entries.label: Tell us why you are interested in building an engineering career at Datadog.
entries.value: The work I have done most recently maps closely onto what I understand Datadog to be building. At Summer Atlantic Capital I own major parts of the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system, including the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, temporal sequence modeling over event streams, and a learning-to-rank layer for ordering alerts. The lesson that stuck with me is that detection alone is not the product. A system that fires too many alerts hands an analyst a second problem instead of solving the first, so prioritization, explanation quality, and documented failure modes matter as much as model accuracy. I also built a retrieval-augmented explanation layer so outputs read as something a human can act on. I want an engineering career where reliability and operational usefulness are the actual measure of good work, and where an intern is expected to own a real piece of a system rather than isolated tickets. Datadog is one of the few places where infrastructure scale and that kind of judgment about alerts are the daily problem.
